title: Environment protection law reform (EPBC) and National EPA
summary: Environment protection reform bills passed on 28 November 2025 and received assent on 1 December 2025; a National EPA was to start on 1 July 2026, with the rest by 1 December 2026.
direction_rationale: Faster, more certain approvals lower barriers for new projects, while stricter national standards raise compliance costs.

verified.notes: Assent 1 Dec 2025 confirmed on the Federal Register (Environment Protection Reform Act 2025, registered 2 Dec 2025). Tranche 1 (20 Feb 2026) and the National EPA's establishment (1 Jul 2026) are from DCCEEW's 'Progress on implementation' page, as reported in search results (fact-check, 6 Nov 2026); DCCEEW says the remaining reforms commence on or before 1 Dec 2026. Not read on the register.

review.notes: Drafted by AI-assisted desk research on 18 October 2026 (legislation gap scan, docs/legislation_gap_scan.md) from the sources cited. Not yet checked by a person: verify dates, industries and the direction hypothesis before use.

assessment.summary: Reforms to national environment law and a new National EPA promise faster, more certain approvals alongside stricter national standards. The productivity effect depends on standards and processes still being made.

marks.reason: Faster, more certain approvals lower the cost of delay for new projects.
Stricter national environmental standards add compliance requirements.

responsible.note: Administers the Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Act 1999. The reforms create a National EPA; its start was not checked.
